newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel oil steady, quiet, ignores fall in crude.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel oil steady, quiet, ignores fall in crude.

text.p: European fuel markets were steady in quiet trade on Wednesday morning, mostly ignoring the fall in crude, traders said.
High sulphur fuel barges began slightly softer at $82.50 and $82.75 before picking up. Deals at $84 and $84.50 a tonne were heard in Antwerp later in the morning. Bunker demand was limited.
One percent cracked cargoes were little discussed with swaps flat and no prompt to push the market down.
"Its not as bad as I expected it would be, given crude's fall," said one seller. "It seems to have found some support from somewhere, with numbers the same as yesterday."
"But it seems everyone is in a bit of a lull, they are not too interested even in giving out price indications because of market uncertainty," he added.

In the Mediterranean the fuel market was digesting the impact of Italian barrels loading June 15-17 sold trader to trader for a price heard to be around $75.50 fob. Both parties were believed pricing large cargo purchases this month.
